title: M'Goun & Lakes traverse (Morocco option)
summary: Demnate to Boumalne Dadès across the M'Goun massif and the lake plateau — Aït Bouguemez, the Ahansal gorges, Imilchil and the Dadès. 491 km and 12,290 m over 7 days — 70 km and 1,756 m a day, 53% paved / 47% unpaved. One-way, Demnate to Boumalne Dadès.
season: Best Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct · the high plateau is snowbound in winter

days.title: Demnate → Aït Mhamed
days.summary: Out of Demnate on farm pistes onto the Aït Mhamed plateau — half the day off tarmac.

days.title: Aït Mhamed → Tabant
days.summary: Over the rim into Aït Bouguemez, the Happy Valley. Almost entirely piste, topping 2,613 m.

days.title: Tabant → Zaouiat Ahansal
days.summary: The big crossing to Zaouiat Ahansal at 2,930 m — the highest point of the option, nearly all off-road.

days.title: Zaouiat Ahansal → Anergui
days.summary: Down through the Ahansal gorges to Anergui, again mostly piste.

days.title: Anergui → Imilchil
days.summary: The paved recovery: valley road up to the lakes at Imilchil, but 2,224 m of it.

days.title: Imilchil → Agoudal → Msemrir
days.summary: Long plateau day on tarmac past Agoudal and Aït Hani to Msemrir.

days.title: Msemrir → Boumalne Dadès
days.summary: Off the plateau to Boumalne on a mix of piste and road down the Dadès.

title: Ahansal & Happy Valley loop (Morocco option)
summary: A closed loop from Demnate through Bin el Ouidane, the Ahansal gorges and Aït Bouguemez. 408 km and 9,779 m over 5 days — 82 km and 1,956 m a day, 50% paved / 50% unpaved. Closed loop from Demnate.
season: Best Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct · Ahansal gorges flood after heavy rain

days.title: Demnate → Azilal → Bin el Ouidane
days.summary: North to the Bin el Ouidane reservoir through Azilal — the roadiest day.

days.title: Bin el Ouidane → Zaouiat Ahansal
days.summary: The crux: 104 km and 3,445 m into Zaouiat Ahansal, about half of it off tarmac.

days.title: Zaouiat Ahansal → Tabant
days.summary: Over the 2,930 m col into Aït Bouguemez, almost pure piste.

days.title: Tabant → Aït Mhamed
days.summary: The Happy Valley piste west to Aït Mhamed.

days.title: Aït Mhamed → Azilal → Demnate
days.summary: Rolling run back through Azilal to close the loop at Demnate.

title: Toubkal to Telouet (Morocco option)
summary: Asni to Demnate across the western High Atlas — Toubkal foothills, the Amizmiz piste, then Tizi n'Tichka and Telouet. 454 km and 12,004 m over 6 days — 76 km and 2,001 m a day, 49% paved / 51% unpaved. One-way, Asni to Demnate.
season: Best Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct · Tizi n’Test closes in snow

days.title: Asni → Ouirgane → Ijoukak
days.summary: Gentle opener down the Ouirgane valley to Ijoukak, mostly sealed.

days.title: Ijoukak → Amizmiz
days.summary: North over the hills to Amizmiz, a third off-road.

days.title: Amizmiz → Asni
days.summary: The classic piste back east to Asni — 92% unpaved, the most off-road day of all three options.

days.title: Asni → Tighza
days.summary: The monster: 129 km and 3,863 m east to Tighza, split evenly between tarmac and track.

days.title: Tighza → Telouet
days.summary: Piste-heavy climb up to Telouet.

days.title: Telouet → Demnate
days.summary: Long finish over the Tichka side to Demnate, two thirds off tarmac.

title: Taşeli traverse (Taurus option)
summary: Antalya to Mersin the inland way — over Alacabel onto the Konya plateau, east across the Taşeli plateau through Ermenek, down the Göksu to the sea and back up to Arslanköy for the last day. 726 km and 11,998 m over 7 days — 104 km and 1,714 m a day, tarmac throughout, one-way Antalya → Mersin.
season: Best late Apr–Jun and mid-Sep–end Oct · the plateau above 1,500 m takes its first snow in November and the passes can close by December

days.title: Antalya → Akseki
days.summary: Out of Kaleiçi along the Pamphylian plain to Manavgat, where the D695 turns inland and climbs a thousand metres to Akseki. Flat for 75 km, then all of the day's work in the last 60.
days.stayingAt: Akseki — or Ormana, 12 km off-route, for the düğmeli ev guesthouses

days.title: Akseki → Alacabel → Bozkır
days.summary: The pass day. Alacabel at 1,825 m is the high point of the whole Antalya–Konya road; beyond it the mountains give way to the Konya plateau at Seydişehir, and a rolling 55 km east ends at Bozkır.
highlights: First night on the Konya side

days.title: Bozkır → Hadim → Taşkent
days.summary: Short and steep: down into the Göksu gorge at Yerköprü, then straight back up 700 m to Hadim, the highest district town in Konya. Half a day in hand for the waterfall and the tufa bridges.
days.stayingAt: Hadim (1,530 m) or Taşkent, 10 km on
highlights: The short day — take the afternoon off

days.title: Taşkent → Sarıveliler → Ermenek
days.summary: Over the provincial crest at about 1,850 m onto the Taşeli plateau, then a shelf road along the mountainside through Sarıveliler and Başyayla to Ermenek. Nothing all day is below 1,200 m.

days.title: Ermenek → Mut
days.summary: Down to the Ermenek dam and the Göksu, over one more ridge, then off the plateau altogether to Mut at 275 m — apricots, Roman bridges and the first warm night since the coast.

days.title: Mut → Silifke → Erdemli
days.summary: The recovery day: the whole Göksu canyon downhill to Silifke, then east along the coast past Kızkalesi. Long, but the only day under 1,100 m of climbing.

days.title: Erdemli → Güzeloluk → Arslanköy → Mersin
days.summary: The sting in the tail: 1,400 m out of Erdemli onto the Bolkar shelf, across the yayla road to Arslanköy at 1,475 m, then a 40 km descent into Mersin.

title: Coast & cols (Taurus option)
region: Central Taurus and the Cilician coast, Türkiye
summary: The same crossing with its feet in the sea: coast to Alanya, then straight up to 1,800 m, over the Taşeli plateau to Ermenek, back down to the Mediterranean at Anamur, along the wildest stretch of the D400, and up the escarpment one last time. 732 km and 12,423 m over 7 days — 105 km and 1,775 m a day, one-way Antalya → Mersin.
season: Best late Apr–Jun and mid-Sep–end Oct · the plateau above 1,500 m takes its first snow in November and the passes can close by December

days.title: Antalya → Side → Alanya
days.summary: Flat and fast down the D400 past Side to Alanya. The only easy day of the week, and in late October the sea is still about 25 °C.

days.title: Alanya → Taşkent
days.summary: Sea level to about 1,800 m in one go. The Alanya–Konya road leaves the Dim valley and climbs without a real break to the crest above Söbüçimen before settling onto the plateau at Taşkent.

days.title: Taşkent → Sarıveliler → Ermenek
days.summary: Over the provincial crest at about 1,850 m and along the Taşeli shelf road through Sarıveliler and Başyayla to Ermenek.

days.title: Ermenek → Gezende → Anamur
days.summary: Down the Ermenek river past the Gezende dam and out to the Mediterranean at Anamur — 1,250 m to sea level through a gorge, on one of the best descents in the country.

days.title: Anamur → Aydıncık → Silifke
days.summary: The wild stretch of the D400: headland after headland, banana greenhouses, new viaducts. Drivers use the tunnels, which leaves the old coast road quiet — but check each tunnel before committing to it.
highlights: Tunnels: take the old road round

days.title: Silifke → Uzuncaburç → Kırobası → Arslanköy
days.summary: Back up the escarpment to Roman Diocaesarea at Uzuncaburç, then the plateau road north-east through Kırobası and Güzeloluk to Arslanköy. Sea level to 1,475 m with three ridges in between.
days.stayingAt: Arslanköy (1,475 m) — dağ evi accommodation, book ahead

days.title: Arslanköy → Fındıkpınarı → Mersin
days.summary: A short last morning: across to Fındıkpınarı and then 1,200 m down to the sea, with the afternoon free for the train to Adana.

title: The six-day line (Taurus option)
summary: The Taşeli traverse with a day taken out: the same road from Antalya to Mersin, split six ways instead of seven. 726 km and 11,677 m over 6 days — 121 km and 1,946 m a day. Nothing is cut except rest; two of the six days carry more than 2,000 m.
season: Best late Apr–Jun and mid-Sep–end Oct · the plateau above 1,500 m takes its first snow in November and the passes can close by December

days.title: Antalya → Akseki
days.summary: Out of Kaleiçi along the Pamphylian plain to Manavgat, then the D695 inland and a thousand metres up to Akseki.

days.title: Akseki → Alacabel → Bozkır
days.summary: Alacabel at 1,825 m, the high point of the Antalya–Konya road, then Seydişehir and the plateau edge east to Bozkır.
highlights: First night on the Konya side

days.title: Bozkır → Taşkent → Sarıveliler
days.summary: The Göksu gorge at Yerköprü, the wall up to Hadim, then the crest onto the Taşeli plateau. The day the six-day version costs you.
days.stayingAt: Sarıveliler (1,650 m) — beds are thin, ring ahead or push on to Ermenek

days.title: Sarıveliler → Ermenek → Mut
days.summary: Off the plateau in one push: Ermenek for lunch, the dam gorge below it, then the long drop to Mut at 275 m.

days.title: Mut → Silifke → Erdemli
days.summary: The Göksu canyon downhill to Silifke and east along the coast past Kızkalesi — the one day that is not a mountain day.

days.title: Erdemli → Güzeloluk → Arslanköy → Mersin
days.summary: 1,400 m out of Erdemli onto the Bolkar shelf, across to Arslanköy at 1,475 m, then the long descent into Mersin.

title: Around Manaslu
summary: Ten days trekking the Manaslu approach, 21–30 October 2025 — 160.5 km and 7,606 m from Machhakhola up the Budhi Gandaki to Samdo, with an acclimatisation day to Manaslu Base Camp at 4,855 m, then back out the same valley. These tracks do not cross Larke La: Samdo is the furthest point and day 8 turns around.

days.title: Machhakhola → Jagat
days.summary: Into the Budhi Gandaki gorge — 18.5 km and 803 m, climbing from 888 m to Jagat at 1,352 m.

days.title: Jagat → Deng
days.summary: Longer and steadier up the valley, 19.6 km to Deng at 1,877 m.

days.title: Deng → Namrung
days.summary: The valley narrows and steepens: 1,243 m of climbing over 16.6 km to Namrung at 2,647 m.

days.title: Namrung → Shyala
days.summary: Through Lho with the first big mountain views, finishing at Shyala at 3,522 m.
highlights: Over 3,500 m for the first time

days.title: Shyala → Samagaon
days.summary: Short on paper but the track climbs to 4,055 m on a side excursion before dropping into Samagaon at 3,537 m.

days.title: Samagaon → Manaslu Base Camp → Samagaon
days.summary: Acclimatisation day: out and back from Samagaon to Manaslu Base Camp at 4,855 m — the highest point of the whole trek and its biggest climbing day at 1,356 m.
highlights: High point 4,855 m — highest of the trek

days.title: Samagaon → Samdo
days.summary: Shortest day of the trek at 8.1 km, up to Samdo at 3,869 m — the furthest point reached.

days.title: Samdo → Lho
days.summary: Turning back down the valley, 15.6 km of almost pure descent to Lho at 3,181 m.

days.title: Lho → Bihi
days.summary: Longest day of the trek: 21.9 km retracing the approach down to Bihi at 2,163 m.

days.title: Bihi → Chisopani
days.summary: Last day out, 15.3 km down to Chisopani at 1,692 m.

title: Around Cyprus
summary: Six days riding a full loop of Cyprus, 30 November to 5 December 2025 — 618.9 km and 7,024 m, anticlockwise from Peyia over the Troodos, along the Karpas peninsula and back down the south coast. Recorded on Strava, cleaned and simplified for the web.

days.title: Peyia → Pedoulas
days.summary: Straight off the coast and up into the Troodos — 2,131 m of climbing to Pedoulas at 1,248 m, the hardest day of the loop by a distance.

days.title: Pedoulas → Templos
days.summary: Long descent off the mountains to the north coast. A late start and only 500 m of climbing — the recovery day.

days.title: Templos → Rizokarpaso
days.summary: Out along the Karpas peninsula. Flat and exposed — nothing above 158 m all day.

days.title: Rizokarpaso → Ayia Napa
days.summary: Back down the peninsula and around to the south-east coast. A short burst of GPS jitter has been removed.

days.title: Ayia Napa → Pano Lefkara
days.summary: Shortest day, turning inland off the coast and climbing gently to Lefkara.

days.title: Pano Lefkara → Peyia
days.summary: The long way home: 131.8 km and 1,853 m back across to Peyia, closing the loop. Started at 05:31.

title: French Alps traverse
summary: Six days by bike from the Massif des Maures to Grenoble — 599.8 km and 9,972 m of climbing, crossing from the Mediterranean hinterland into the high Alps. Tracks are the recorded Garmin files, cleaned and simplified for the web.

days.title: La Garde-Freinet → Castellane
days.summary: Out of the Massif des Maures and into the Gorges du Verdon approach. The longest low-altitude day — the climbing is constant but never goes above 1,000 m.

days.title: Castellane → Barcelonnette
days.summary: First real altitude of the trip: the route tops out at 2,246 m before dropping into the Ubaye valley.

days.title: Barcelonnette → Briançon
days.summary: Shortest day by distance, and still 1,617 m of climbing. Tops out at 2,115 m.

days.title: Briançon → Le Bourg-d'Oisans
days.summary: The high point of the whole trip at 2,641 m. GPS dropped out several times on this stage (tunnels and deep valley sections) — the track runs straight across those gaps rather than guessing a line, and a short burst of GPS jitter has been removed.
highlights: High point 2,641 m — highest of the trip

days.title: Le Bourg-d'Oisans → Albertville
days.summary: Long valley day north through the Maurienne side, 108.6 km with a 1,926 m high point.

days.title: Albertville → Grenoble
days.summary: Biggest day of the trip: 117.5 km and 2,025 m of climbing to finish, all of it below 1,350 m.
